nodes.title: Note:
widgets_values:
Nano Banana - inpaint v3 (aioli-nodes >= 1.8.0, tested on ComfyUI 0.43.2).
v3 = v2 + 📏 Resolution Panel. Same render as v2.

One path, no ENABLE INPAINT / MASKING.

- Drawn mask (or PROMPT MASKING / SAM3): inpaint per region, crop + padding.
- Mask + CONTEXT = full_image: Gemini sees the whole image, only the masked zones are pasted back.
- No mask: the whole image is edited.
- OUTPAINT RATIO: only the new bands are generated (+ REGENERATE WHOLE IMAGE: bands + whole image).

📏 RESOLUTION PANEL (left): OUTPUT SCALE, OUTPAINT RATIO, REGENERATE WHOLE IMAGE, MODEL SIZE, multiple, SQUARE, SHRINK BIG CROPS, padding and CONTEXT are set there and feed the subgraph. Its diagram follows your settings before any run (regions from the drawn mask), then shows the exact values of the run.
OUTPUT SCALE: factor on the source. MODEL SIZE: crop size sent to Gemini (square equivalent).
SQUARE on -> aspect 1:1, off -> auto (for outpaint, SQUARE off is usually better). GEMINI RESOLUTION (subgraph): 1K / 2K / 4K output.

---

NANO BANANA - REGLAGES
API Google (cloud) : pas de NDA dans ce wf.
ENABLE NANO BANANA off = test du graphe sans appel API (le batch d'entree passe tel quel).
Inpaint : crop carre (SQUARE du panneau) -> aspect 1:1 envoye a Gemini. Image entiere : auto.
Taille : MODEL SIZE 1024 avec GEMINI RESOLUTION 1K (2048 avec 2K) = sortie a la taille du crop, pas de reechantillonnage.
Refs 2 / 3 : batchees a la taille du crop (Batch Images), donc recadrees au centre.
seed : force le re-run, le resultat Gemini n'est pas deterministe.
Plusieurs masques = un appel API par region.

USE LLM PROMPT ENHANCE
When enabled, use the LLM Prompt Enhance feature to enhance your prompt.

ENABLE PROMPT MASKING
Automatically generates masks in the image using SAM3. 

PROMPT MASKING
To prompt multiple subjects separately, use commas to separate prompts and specify the maximum number of objects to detect for each prompt using the :N syntax.

For example above test prompt finds 2 cakes, one apron, 4 window panels

```
eye:2, window panels:4
```

USE LLM AUTOMATIC MASKING
When enabled, automatically generate masks using the LLM. If not empty, it can use your manual prompt masking as guidance for elements to mask.

You are an expert image-generation engine. You must ALWAYS produce an image.
Interpret all user input—regardless of format, intent, or abstraction—as literal visual directives for image composition.
If a prompt is conversational or lacks specific visual details, you must creatively invent a concrete visual scenario that depicts the concept.
Prioritize generating the visual representation above any text, formatting, or conversational requests.

widgets_values:
You are a prompt writer for Google's Gemini image-editing model (Nano Banana / Nano Banana Pro).

You receive:

* a raw user instruction
* an image to edit

Rewrite the instruction into a clear editing prompt that applies naturally to the image content.

Rules, in priority order:

1. Output only the final prompt, in English.
2. Preserve the user's requested edit exactly while improving clarity and specificity. Do not add objects, styles, actions, or details that were not requested.
3. Use the image only to identify the subjects or elements affected by the requested edit.
4. Refer to visible subjects using simple, factual descriptions.
5. Rewrite for clarity and specificity, not creativity — in natural sentences, like briefing a professional retoucher, never as keywords or tags.
6. Keep the edit limited to what the instruction targets; do not alter unrelated content. State the scope explicitly when it helps.
7. Unless explicitly requested otherwise, preserve the original lighting, colours, perspective, composition and visual style so the edit blends naturally into the image.
8. Keep any quoted text and hexadecimal colour codes exactly as provided.

widgets_values:
You segment objects in an image.

Read STRICT_FILTER and output only objects that match it.
If STRICT_FILTER is empty, list all distinct foreground objects.
STRICT_FILTER decides which objects to keep; the formatting rules below always apply.

Rules:
1. Output only objects that match STRICT_FILTER; ignore everything else.
2. If unsure whether an object matches STRICT_FILTER, leave it out.
3. Never output the background, sky, ground, walls, or empty areas.
4. When several instances of the same object type are present, write the label once followed by :N, where N is how many you see. If unsure, give the higher number — N is only an upper limit, so overestimating is better than underestimating.
5. Use singular lowercase labels, separated by commas. No sentences, no explanation, no final period.
6. At most 10 labels.
7. Order by importance, most important first
8. If nothing matches, output exactly: none

Example: person, dog, hat:2, window panel:4

STRICT_FILTER:

nodes.title: GEMMA keywords -> SAM3
widgets_values: Look at the image and list the distinct subjects/objects to segment. Output ONLY lowercase nouns separated by commas, no sentences, no explanation, no final period. Max 32 tokens total. If several instances of the same thing exist, append :N with N the count (e.g. 'window panel:4, cake:2'). ORDER them from MOST important and LARGEST to least important and smallest, foreground first. Do NOT include the background, sky or empty areas as an item. Example: person, dog, hat, window panel:3

Max 32 tokens total. If several instances of the same thing exist, append :N with N the count (e.g. 'window panel:4, cake:2'). ORDER them from MOST important and LARGEST to least important and smallest, foreground first. Do NOT include the background, sky or empty areas as an item. Example: person, dog, hat, window panel:3

nodes.title: Note: Prompt format
widgets_values:
Max tokens for this model is only 32, to separately prompt multiple subjects you can separate prompts with comma, and set the max amount of objects detected for each prompt with :N

For example above test prompt finds 2 cakes, one apron, 4 window panels
